newsitem.title: USA: US yields to rise if foreigners don't buy-Fidelity.
newsitem.headline: US yields to rise if foreigners don't buy-Fidelity.

text.p: U.S. interest rates would probably rise if foreign investors substantially cut back on their purchases of U.S. Treasury securities, a senior Fidelity Investments official said on Thursday.

"The favorable interest rate environment that we have enjoyed in the United States is vulnerable to the vagaries of investing by foreigners," Robert Pozen, Fidelity Managing Director and General Counsel, said.
"If they substantially reduced their purchases of U.S. Treasury securities," he added, "the interest rate on such securities would probably rise."

In prepared testimony to the Senate Finance Committee, Pozen said that foreign investors accounted for 31.6 percent of total private holdings of U.S. Treasuries at the end of last year, up from 21.7 percent at the end of 1994.
"Japanese savers have been avid buyers of U.S. Treasury securities," he added. Japan investors are the largest foreign owners of Treasuries, with $271.7 billion worth of holdings.

"But what if the Japanese economy recovered and Japanese short-term interest rates rose to three or four percent?" Pozen asked. "The Japanese appetite for U.S. Treasury securities would surely diminish."
